clusters.name: Sewa, Harga & Paket
clusters.theme: Someone who has already decided to rent a photobooth and is now trying to find out what it costs before they contact anyone.
clusters.note: The money cluster. Every query here is a person with an event date already in their calendar, and every one of them is currently being answered by a WhatsApp number instead of a page.

clusters.name: Cakupan Wilayah Jakarta
clusters.theme: Checking whether a vendor actually serves their specific part of Jakarta before wasting a conversation.
clusters.note: All five administrative regions autocomplete on their own, which means Jakarta is not one market here - it is five, and coverage is a real purchase objection.

clusters.name: Tipe & Gaya Booth
clusters.theme: Comparing booth formats and aesthetics to work out which one suits their event before shortlisting a vendor.
clusters.note: The only genuine evaluation stage in the whole harvest. Format names - 360, analog, high angle - are doing the work that brand names do in other markets.

clusters.name: Venue & Brand Spesifik
clusters.theme: Looking for one named operator or one named venue's booth, not for a category.
clusters.note: Do not chase these with commercial pages - the searcher wants a specific brand. Worth watching as a competitor list, not as a content target.

coverageGaps: Nobody publishes an actual price range - every result pushes the searcher into a WhatsApp chat before revealing a number
No page maps which vendors genuinely cover which Jakarta region, despite all five regions autocompleting separately
The difference between 360, analog and standard booths is never explained in terms of what a guest actually experiences
Wedding-specific logistics (venue access, setup time, operator count) are absent even though wedding queries carry the highest commercial weight
